Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

Testing the E6 cut more carefully, I see it only has two liberties at E7 and F6 after white's stones surround it, making it vulnerable to atari, so that line looks bad. Tracing liberties, if I cut at E3 white can atari me quickly with either E2 or F3, since my cutting stone would only have two liberties, so this cut doesn't work immediately.

Instead, playing F3 first seems better — it stakes out the bottom-right and sets up the E3 cut as a follow-up threat, likely forcing white to defend at E3 and solidify their bottom wall, after which I can shift attention to D6 or E6 at the top, though D7 might then slide further with C5.

I'm also checking my left-side group's safety: C3, C4, D4, D5 have five liberties total (B3, C2, B4, C5, D6), so they seem reasonably secure for now even if white probes around there.

Weighing D6 as the more straightforward move — it blocks white from encircling my left side and puts pressure on white's D7 stone, which would then need to fight for life near the top where my G6 stone is waiting; after D6, white likely responds with E6 to block, building a wall from D2 up to E6 plus D7, and I'd consider C7 to pressure D7 further depending on whether it connects diagonally to E6.

I'm also looking at G4, which works with G6 to claim the right side and part of the bottom-right, though white could respond with F3 and secure roughly rows 1-2 across columns E-G on the bottom.

After all that, I'm circling back to D6 as the solid, safe choice that holds the top-left, even though it concedes something to white on the other side.

Weighing a standard idea: since black's left group already has decent strength with five liberties and a corner, the biggest move is really F3/G3 at the bottom-right, since it also pressures white's bottom group by threatening the cut at E3 — forcing a response and giving me sente to follow up with D6 or C6. If white hanes at F4 in reply, my F3 stone still keeps three liberties, and the resulting E3 cut turns into a tight liberty race that favors whoever moves first, which is messy but workable. I'm settling on F3.
